w-in-041.title: Bread Upma (Indian Bread)

instructions.1: Toast the bread slices in a pan or toaster until golden brown and crispy.
instructions.2: Cut the bread slices into small cubes and set aside.
instructions.3: Heat the oil in a large pan.
instructions.4: Add the mustard seeds and curry leaves and let the mustard seeds pop.
instructions.5: Add the onion, ginger paste, and green chili and sauté until the onion becomes translucent.
instructions.6: Add the tomatoes and sauté until they become soft.
instructions.7: Add the turmeric, Kashmiri red chili powder, sugar, and salt and sauté for a minute on low heat.
instructions.8: Add the bell pepper and sauté for a minute.
instructions.9: Add the water and mix well.
instructions.10: Add the toasted bread cubes and gently mix until the bread absorbs the spices.
instructions.11: Cover the pan and cook on low heat for 2-3 minutes.
instructions.12: Serve the bread upma garnished with coriander leaves.

w-in-041.culturalNotes: Bread upma is a popular dish in South India, often served as a breakfast or appetizer.

w-in-042.title: Indian Pickled Onions

w-in-042-i8.name: Beetroot
w-in-042-i8.standardAmount: ¼ medium beetroot (a small wedge, optional)

instructions.1: Peel all the red pearl onions. This is the most time-consuming step in the recipe.
instructions.2: Make a slit in each peeled onion lengthwise using a paring knife without cutting it all the way through. Transfer all the onions to an 8 oz mason jar.
instructions.3: In a pan on medium heat, add water with salt, sugar, cinnamon stick, cloves, peppercorns, and beetroot (optional, this gives the onions a deep pink color).
instructions.4: Boil this mixture on medium heat for 3-4 minutes until the salt and sugar dissolve and the color of the water changes to red (because of the beetroot). Then remove the pan from the stove and let the mixture cool down for 10 minutes.
instructions.5: After it has cooled down, add white vinegar and stir. Now, pour this pickling liquid into the mason jar with onions, making sure the onions are submerged in the mixture. Shake the jar.
instructions.6: Refrigerate for 24 hours and then enjoy! These pickled onions should stay good in the fridge for 3-4 weeks.

w-in-042.culturalNotes: Indian pickled onions are a popular dish in Indian cuisine, served as a side dish or with main courses.

w-in-043.title: Jhunka (Zunka) with Bhakri

instructions.1: Heat 2 tbsp of oil in a large kadai, and add 1 tsp of mustard seeds, 1 tsp of cumin, and a pinch of asafoetida. Let them splutter.
instructions.2: Add 4 cloves of finely chopped garlic, 1 finely chopped chili, and sauté well.
instructions.3: Add 1 finely chopped onion and sauté until it changes color slightly.
instructions.4: Add ¼ tsp of turmeric, 1 tsp of Kashmiri red chili powder, and 1 tsp of salt. Sauté slightly without burning the spices.
instructions.5: Add 1 cup of gram flour and sauté on low flame for 5 minutes, or until the flour turns golden and aromatic.
instructions.6: Sprinkle ¼ cup of water and mix well. Continue sprinkling water in batches until the mixture turns moist.
instructions.7: Cover and simmer for 10 minutes, or until the gram flour is cooked completely.
instructions.8: Stir well to ensure there are no lumps.
instructions.9: Add the chopped coriander leaves and serve the zunka with bhakri.

w-in-043.culturalNotes: Jhunka (Zunka) is a popular dish in Maharashtra, India, typically served with bhakri (whole wheat flatbread).

w-in-044.title: Noodles Kathi Roll

instructions.1: Heat a pan over medium heat and add 3 tbsp of oil, then add 1 tbsp of green onions and stir.
instructions.2: Add ¼ cup of bell pepper and 1 cup of chopped cauliflower and stir for a minute.
instructions.3: Add 2 tbsp of soy sauce and ¼ tsp of salt, and continue stirring for a minute.
instructions.4: Add the cooked noodles and gently mix with the sauce, then add 2 tbsp of green onions and stir well.
instructions.5: Heat a pan over medium heat and add ½ tsp of butter, then add the chapati and roast until golden brown.
instructions.6: Add 1 tsp of soy sauce and 1 tsp of tomato sauce on the chapati, then place a tablespoon of noodles in the center.
instructions.7: Sprinkle a little chaat masala powder, then roll the chapati tightly.
instructions.8: Wrap the kathi roll in aluminum foil or butter paper.

w-in-044.culturalNotes: Kathi roll is a popular street food in India, often served as a snack or quick lunch.

w-in-045.title: Kheer (Rice Pudding)

instructions.1: Bring the milk to a boil in a pot over medium heat, stirring regularly to prevent scorching.
instructions.2: Add the rice and simmer slowly until thick (about 20 minutes).
instructions.3: Stir in the sugar, sultanas, and ground cardamom seeds. Cook for 5 minutes.
instructions.4: Remove the pot from the heat, stir in the almonds and rosewater, and cover until ready to serve.

w-in-045.culturalNotes: Kheer is a traditional Indian dessert, often served on special occasions.

w-in-046.title: Khichdi

instructions.1: Wash the rice and lentils and soak them in water for 10-15 minutes.
instructions.2: Add salt and turmeric powder.
instructions.3: Cook in a pressure cooker with 3-4 cups of water.
instructions.4: After the first whistle, reduce the heat and cook for 4-5 more minutes.
instructions.5: Allow to cool before serving. Serve with ghee or buttermilk.

w-in-046.culturalNotes: Khichdi is a popular dish in India, served as a light meal or main course.

w-in-047.title: Amritsari Aloo Kulcha

instructions.1: Mix the maida, baking powder, baking soda, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
instructions.2: Add the curd and water gradually and knead the dough until it is smooth and consistent.
instructions.3: Cover the dough and let it rest for 30 minutes.
instructions.4: In another bowl, mix the grated potatoes, finely chopped onions, chilli powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, aamchur, ajwain, salt, kala namak, ginger paste, finely chopped chillies, and finely chopped coriander.
instructions.5: Shape the dough into small balls and roll each ball using a rolling pin.
instructions.6: Place a spoonful of the filling in the center of each flattened dough and seal the edges tightly.
instructions.7: Heat the tawa and add a little ghee, then place the kulcha and fry until golden brown on both sides.
instructions.8: Serve hot with your favorite chutneys.

w-in-047.culturalNotes: Kulcha is a traditional Indian bread from the city of Amritsar, typically served on the streets with the preferred filling.

w-in-048.title: Almond Laddu

instructions.1: In a pan, dry roast 1 cup almonds until they turn crunchy and golden brown.
instructions.2: Cool completely and transfer to a blender.
instructions.3: Blend to a fine powder by pulsing a few times.
instructions.4: Transfer the powder to a large bowl and set aside.
instructions.5: Now, dry roast 1 cup dry coconut until it turns golden brown.
instructions.6: Transfer the roasted coconut to a blender along with ¾ cup jaggery.
instructions.7: Blend to a coarse powder by pulsing a few times.
instructions.8: Transfer the powder to the same bowl of almond powder.
instructions.9: Add ¼ tsp cardamom powder and mix well.
instructions.10: In a pan, heat 2 tbsp ghee and roast 10 cashews and 2 tbsp raisins.
instructions.11: Roast until the cashews turn golden brown.
instructions.12: Pour the roasted dry fruits into the ladoo mixture.
instructions.13: Mix well to ensure the mixture is moist.
instructions.14: Grease your hands with ghee and start shaping the ladoo.
instructions.15: Enjoy the almond ladoo for 2 weeks when stored in an airtight container.

w-in-048.culturalNotes: Laddu is a traditional Indian sweet served on special occasions and celebrations.

w-in-049.title: Naan

instructions.1: Knead all the ingredients with enough water (approximately ¾ cup) to make the dough.
instructions.2: Wrap the dough in a damp muslin cloth and let it rise for 2-3 hours.
instructions.3: Divide the dough into small balls.
instructions.4: Roll out the balls into oblong or round shapes using a rolling pin or by hand.
instructions.5: Smear the surface with water and bake in a tandoor or preheated oven (as hot as your oven will go).
instructions.6: The naans should puff up a little and be ready to remove from the oven in 4-5 minutes.
instructions.7: Brush the naan with butter and serve hot.

w-in-049.culturalNotes: Naan is a traditional Indian bread baked in a tandoor oven. It is typically served with main dishes.

w-in-050.title: Aloo Cheese Paratha

instructions.1: Knead the flour with water and salt until the dough is smooth and elastic. Cover the dough and let it rest for 15 minutes.
instructions.2: In a bowl, mix the mashed potato with the chopped onion, ginger, coriander, salt, Kashmiri chilli powder, chaat masala, and dry mango powder. Add the shredded mozzarella cheese and mix well.
instructions.3: Take a piece of dough and roll it out on a floured surface. Place a spoonful of the filling in the center of the dough and seal it into a round shape.
instructions.4: Roll out the paratha with a rolling pin until it is thin. Place it on a hot skillet and cook until golden brown on both sides.
instructions.5: Repeat the process with the remaining dough and filling. Serve hot with yogurt or a spicy sauce.

w-in-050.culturalNotes: Paratha is a traditional Indian dish, often served as a breakfast or light lunch.

w-tr-001.title: Adana Kebab

w-tr-001-i1.name: Lamb meat from leg of lamb

instructions.1: Combine the lamb meat cubes and tail fat cubes using a mezzaluna knife. It will take about 30 minutes to mix the meat and fat well.
instructions.2: After mixing the meat and fat well, the mixture will look like ground meat.
instructions.3: Add the mezzaluna-cut red carmen pepper, red hot chili pepper flakes, and salt to the mixture and use the mezzaluna knife again to mix all the ingredients well. It will take an additional 10 minutes to mix the mixture well.
instructions.4: Put the kebab meat on the skewers. You can use water to prevent the kebab meat from sticking to your hands while putting the meat on the skewers.
instructions.5: Place the skewers on a charcoal grill and cook for 15-20 minutes. While grilling, don't forget to flip each side of the kebab continuously to keep the fat and ingredients' juices in the meat.

w-tr-001.culturalNotes: Adana Kebab is a famous dish in Turkish cuisine, known for its spicy and strong flavor.

w-tr-002.title: Ali Nazik Kebab

w-tr-002-i8.name: pul biber
w-tr-002-i8.standardAmount: ½ teaspoon (use Aleppo pepper or regular red pepper flakes if you can't find pul biber)

w-tr-002-i10.name: butter
w-tr-002-i10.standardAmount: 30 g / 2 tablespoons (or more if you want)

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 230°C (450°F).
instructions.2: Pierce the eggplants all over with a knife or fork. Pierce the peppers in 1-2 places as well. Place them on an oven rack (or a parchment-lined baking sheet).
instructions.3: Roast for about 15 minutes, or until the peppers are cooked and have a few charred spots.
instructions.4: After 15 minutes, remove the peppers from the oven and turn the eggplants over. Continue roasting for another 25-30 minutes, or until they are very soft.
instructions.5: While the eggplants are roasting, heat a large skillet over high heat. Add the diced lamb in a single layer and cook for 3-4 minutes without stirring.
instructions.6: If you're using a stainless steel pan, don't force the lamb if it sticks. Wait until it releases naturally, then stir. Make sure every piece is turned.
instructions.7: Cook the other side for about 3 minutes.
instructions.8: Add the olive oil and reduce the heat to medium. Cook for 2 more minutes, stirring occasionally. If the lamb releases too much liquid, increase the heat so the liquid evaporates.
instructions.9: Add the salt, paprika, and pul biber. Stir to combine. By this point, the lamb should be tender. Check a piece to make sure. If it isn't tender enough yet, cook it a little longer. Lower the heat if needed to prevent it from drying out.
instructions.10: Add the butter and let it melt completely. Give everything a final stir, then remove the pan from the heat.
instructions.11: Check the eggplants after about 25 minutes (about 40 minutes total). They should be very soft. If not, roast them for another 5 minutes.
instructions.12: Let the eggplants cool until they're easy to handle. Use a knife to scrape the flesh away from the skin. Remove any large dark seeds.
instructions.13: Transfer the eggplant flesh to a strainer. Press with the back of a spoon to remove as much liquid as possible. This gives the mixture a better texture and helps keep the color lighter.
instructions.15: In a medium bowl, combine the strained yogurt, garlic, and salt. Mix well.
instructions.16: Add the finely chopped eggplant and stir until well combined. Taste and add more yogurt and salt if you like.
instructions.17: Spread the eggplant mixture onto a serving plate. Smooth the top with the back of a spoon.
instructions.18: Reheat the lamb over high heat for about 30 seconds. Spoon it over the eggplant yogurt mixture.
instructions.19: Top with the roasted peppers, sprinkle with chopped parsley, and serve immediately.

w-tr-002.culturalNotes: Ali Nazik Kebab is a traditional Turkish dish often served as a main course at family gatherings and celebrations.

w-tr-003.title: Arnavut Ciğeri

instructions.1: Place the onion slices and salt into a small bowl and rub them well to remove the raw red onion's bitterness. Then wash the onion slices and drain them well. Add the sumac and mix it well with the red onion slices, then set aside for garnishing.
instructions.2: Wash and drain the liver well. Then cut the liver into 2 cm (0.8 inches) cubes and put it in a bowl.
instructions.3: In a separate bowl, mix the all-purpose flour, baking powder, and salt.
instructions.4: Place the liver cubes into the flour mixture and make sure they are well coated. Then, take out the liver cubes from the bowl and place them in a strainer to remove the excess flour mixture.
instructions.5: Place the sunflower oil in a deep frying pan and bring the heat to a medium level. To make sure the oil is hot enough for frying, toss a pinch of flour into the frying pan to see if it sizzles. If it does, it means it is ready for frying.
instructions.6: Place the liver cubes in the frying pan and add the red pepper powder, then sauté for about 2-3 minutes. Liver cubes cook very fast, so do not cook them for more than 3 minutes.
instructions.7: Place a paper towel on a plate and then take out the liver cubes from the frying pan with a strainer scoop to remove the excess oil.
instructions.8: Place the liver cubes on a serving plate.
instructions.9: Garnish with the red onion and sumac mixture.

w-tr-003.culturalNotes: Arnavut Ciğeri is a popular dish in Turkey, also known as Albanian liver. It is often served as a main dish on special occasions.

w-tr-004.title: Barbunya Pilaki

instructions.1: Heat the olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the diced onion and cook until translucent.
instructions.2: Add the diced green pepper and cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring often.
instructions.3: Stir in the carrots, cover, and cook for about 5 minutes. Reduce the heat a little if it gets too dry.
instructions.4: Add the tomato paste, stir, then add the potatoes. Cook for a few minutes, stirring often.
instructions.5: Pour in the pureed tomatoes, stir, cover, and cook over medium-low heat for 10-15 minutes, or until the potatoes are tender.
instructions.6: Add the drained borlotti beans, salt, pepper, and hot water. Stir and cook covered for about 5 minutes.
instructions.7: Stir in the mashed garlic and lemon juice, and cook for 1 more minute.
instructions.8: Remove from the heat and let it cool completely in the pan (see Note 3).
instructions.9: Once at room temperature, drizzle with extra olive oil (see Note 4).
instructions.10: Sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve with extra lemon wedges on the side (see Note 5).

w-tr-004.culturalNotes: Barbunya Pilaki is a traditional Turkish dish served as part of a lunch or dinner meal.

w-tr-005.title: Revani (Sweet Semolina Cake)

instructions.1: Mix all the ingredients together until a thick batter forms.
instructions.2: Let the batter rest for 30 minutes to 1 hour.
instructions.3: Grease an 8-inch cake pan and preheat the oven to 325°F (160°C).
instructions.4: Pour the batter into the baking pan, score with the tip of a knife in a diamond pattern, and decorate with slivered almonds.
instructions.5: Bake the cake for 35 minutes, or until cooked through.
instructions.6: Slice the cake along the score lines and set it aside.
instructions.7: On the stovetop, simmer the sugar, lemon juice, rose water, and water for about 5 minutes, or until the sugar dissolves and the kitchen fills with the scent of roses and lemons.
instructions.8: Pour the syrup completely over the sliced cake. It will look like a glass lake, but don’t worry, the cake will soak it up.
instructions.9: Let the cake rest about an hour to let all that sweet, syrupy goodness soak into the cake.

w-tr-005.culturalNotes: Revani is a popular dessert in Turkey, similar to Arabic basbousa but with a special touch of rose water and lemon.

w-tr-006.title: Beyti Kebab

instructions.1: In a large bowl, place the ground beef, breadcrumbs, grated onion, beaten egg, finely pressed garlic, salt, ground cumin, red pepper flakes, and ground black pepper. Mix all ingredients very well. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and let the mixture rest in the fridge for 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
instructions.3: Place baking paper on a large baking pan. Dip your hands in a bowl of water with a drizzle of olive oil to prevent the kofte mix from sticking to your hands. Take a small apple-sized portion of the kofte mixture and shape it into a 12 cm log, gently patting it to flatten. Repeat until all the kofte mixture is used. Place the logs on the baking tray with about 3-4 cm space between them.
instructions.4: Bake the kofte logs in the preheated oven for about 25 minutes.
instructions.5: Once the kofte logs are baked, take the baking tray out of the oven and reduce the oven temperature to 160°C (320°F). Place the kofte logs on a large plate and set aside.
instructions.6: Place and pat the thin flour tortillas over the kofte tray to soak up the kofte juice, then place them on a dry and clean surface.
instructions.7: Place 2 kofte logs end to end on each thin tortilla to make one long roll. Roll them tightly into a log shape. Cut the log into 4 or 5 equal pieces.
instructions.8: Place a clean baking paper on the baking tray and place the tortilla rolls seam-side down on the tray. Brush the top of the tortilla rolls with a little olive oil and bake them for about 5 minutes.
instructions.9: While the tortilla rolls are baking, start preparing the tomato sauce. Pour olive oil into a frying pan and add the chopped garlic. Sauté for about one minute on medium heat. Add the grated tomatoes, tomato paste, and ground red pepper, and combine them well. Simmer on medium to low heat for about 3 minutes.
instructions.10: Prepare the garlic yogurt mix. Combine the chopped garlic with the yogurt and set aside at room temperature.
instructions.11: After the tortilla rolls are baked, remove them from the oven and arrange them in a circle on a serving plate. Place the garlic yogurt mix in the middle of the plate. Drizzle the tomato sauce over the tortilla rolls and the garlic yogurt. Garnish with chopped parsley.

w-tr-006.culturalNotes: Beyti kebab is a popular dish in Turkey, often served on special occasions and family gatherings.

w-tr-007.title: Spicy Braised Eggplant | Burani Bonjon

instructions.1: Slice the eggplant into 1/4-inch thick lengthwise slices. Optionally, salt the eggplant liberally on both sides and place it on a cooling rack over a baking sheet for 15 minutes to draw out bitterness. Rinse the salt off the eggplant and pat dry.
instructions.2: Sauté the minced garlic in olive oil until fragrant in a large, heavy-bottomed skillet. Set the garlic aside in a small container.
instructions.3: Add the vegetable oil to the skillet and heat over medium-high. Add the eggplant and brown, cooking in batches if necessary. The eggplant should be relatively soft when done.
instructions.4: Reduce the heat and add the tomatoes, cilantro, garlic, cayenne, salt, and pepper.
instructions.5: Simmer until the eggplant is very tender, 20-30 minutes.
instructions.6: Garnish with torn cilantro leaves.

w-tr-007.culturalNotes: Boranı is a popular dish in Turkey, served as an appetizer or part of a main meal.

w-tr-008.title: Cabbage Rolls

instructions.1: Cut the cabbage in half vertically and remove the hearts. Put 1 liter of water into a large pot, add 1 tbsp of salt, and bring it to a boil. Place the cabbage leaves in the boiling water until they become tender, then rinse them under cold running water.
instructions.2: Cut away the thick central vein and choose 25 to 30 cabbage leaves that are the size of your palm.
instructions.3: In a large bowl, combine all the filling ingredients with 2 tbsp of olive oil and mix well.
instructions.4: Take one cabbage leaf and place a walnut-sized portion of the filling in the center, then roll it up tightly.
instructions.5: Pour the remaining 2 tbsp of olive oil into a deep and wide saucepan. Arrange the cabbage rolls side by side. Mix the lemon juice and hot water, add a pinch of salt, and pour the mixture over the cabbage rolls. The liquid should come at least halfway up the top layer of rolls. Place a heavy plate over the cabbage rolls to prevent them from unraveling and close the lid. Cook for 40 minutes on medium heat.
instructions.6: After 40 minutes, remove the pot from the heat and let the cabbage rolls rest for about 5 minutes before serving.

w-tr-008.culturalNotes: Cabbage rolls are a traditional dish in Turkish cuisine, often served as a main course at family gatherings.

w-tr-009.title: Turkish Liver Kebabs (Ciğer Şiş)

w-tr-009-i10.name: olive oil (Optional if not using tail fat)

instructions.1: Cut the liver and tail fat into 1-inch cubes.
instructions.2: Thread them onto skewers, one piece of fat followed by two pieces of liver. If you are not using tail fat, brush the liver lightly with olive oil.
instructions.3: In a bowl, combine the sliced onion, sumac, salt, and parsley. Set aside.
instructions.4: Light your charcoal and prepare the grill.
instructions.5: Just before grilling, season both sides of the skewers evenly with salt, cumin, and pul biber.
instructions.6: Grill over hot charcoal, turning occasionally, until nicely charred, about 5 minutes total.
instructions.7: Serve hot with lavash bread, sumac onion salad, and extra cumin and pul biber on the side.

w-tr-009.culturalNotes: Turkish liver kebabs are a traditional dish in Turkish cuisine, often served on special occasions.

w-tr-010.title: Dolma (Stuffed Grape Leaves)

instructions.1: Wash the grape leaves and blanch them in boiling water for 3-5 minutes.
instructions.2: Cut the onions at the bottom root and slice them lengthwise into 1.5 cm thick pieces. Boil for 5-10 minutes until soft, then separate each layer without tearing.
instructions.3: Slice the zucchini and squash lengthwise and hollow them out.
instructions.4: Core the cabbage and boil for 10 minutes, then pull the leaves apart.
instructions.5: Hollow out the hot peppers, tomatoes, and green peppers while keeping their tops.
instructions.6: Combine all the stuffing ingredients in a large bowl.
instructions.7: Stuff the grape leaves: Lay each leaf shiny side down. Place 1 tablespoon of stuffing at the bottom center of the leaf by the stem. Fold the bottom of the leaf up to cover the stuffing. Fold in the sides and roll up in a cylindrical fashion.
instructions.8: Stuff the tomatoes and green peppers, and replace their tops.
instructions.9: Stuff the other vegetables, placing the zucchini and squash on their side and onions (rolled tightly) and tomatoes upright.
instructions.10: Layer the stuffed vegetables in a pot, alternating grape leaves and vegetables. The top layer should be grape leaves.
instructions.11: Mix citric acid and water, and pour over the dolma to just barely cover the top layer of grape leaves.
instructions.12: Put a small plate (inverted) directly on top of the pot of dolma as a weight.
instructions.13: Cover the pot, and cook over high heat for 10 minutes or until it boils.
instructions.14: Once the dolma boils, lower the heat to medium and simmer for about 40 minutes until most of the liquid is absorbed and the rice and meat are cooked.
instructions.15: Remove from heat, and let stand 10 minutes.
instructions.16: Remove the lid and plate. Place a large platter on top of the pot, and using oven mitts, flip the dolma pot onto the platter on top of a table.
instructions.17: Arrange the dolma on the platter as desired and serve.

w-tr-010.culturalNotes: Dolma is a traditional dish in Turkish cuisine, often served as an appetizer or light meal.

w-tr-011.title: Haydari

instructions.1: Place the olive oil in a pan over medium heat, and add the crushed walnut halves and sauté for 2 minutes. Then set it aside and let it cool.
instructions.2: Remove the dill leaves from the stems, rinse them, and then drain the water using a strainer and chop them finely.
instructions.3: Place the feta cheese in a bowl and mash it with a fork.
instructions.4: In a separate bowl, add the strained yogurt, mashed feta cheese, finely chopped dill leaves, dried mint, minced garlic, salt, and sautéed crushed walnut halves, and then mix them well with the fork.
instructions.5: Place the mix on a serving plate.
instructions.6: Serve.

w-tr-011.culturalNotes: Haydari is a traditional Turkish salad served as an appetizer, rich in natural and healthy flavors.

w-tr-012.title: Kalburabastı

instructions.1: In a saucepan, add the water and sugar. Place on medium heat and let it boil for 20 minutes.
instructions.2: Before removing from heat, add the fresh lemon juice and let it boil for 2-3 more minutes. Then set aside until the syrup cools completely to room temperature.
instructions.3: In a bowl, add the unsalted butter, vegetable oil, whole milk, plain yogurt, and semolina and mix them well using a wooden spoon.
instructions.4: Add the flour and baking powder to the mixture using a flour sifter, then knead the mixture well until all ingredients are combined.
instructions.5: After making the dough, cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for 10 minutes.
instructions.6: Take the dough from the refrigerator and divide it into 20 equal pieces. Make small balls.
instructions.7: Take one of the pieces and flatten it gently in your palm or on a clean work surface to give it an oval shape.
instructions.8: Place the oval-shaped dough piece on the grater and fill it with ground walnuts, then seal the ends.
instructions.9: Remove it from the grater and you will see a grid pattern on the surface. Place it on a baking tray.
instructions.10: Repeat the process until all dough balls are finished.
instructions.12: Bake the pieces for 25 minutes until they turn golden brown.
instructions.13: After they turn golden brown, take the baking tray out of the oven and place it on the kitchen counter, then drizzle the room temperature syrup immediately over the pastries.
instructions.14: Leave them to absorb the syrup for 1 hour.
instructions.15: Remove the pastries from the tray and place them in a deep serving plate, then pour the remaining syrup evenly over the pastries using a spoon.
instructions.16: Garnish the pastries with ground pistachios.

w-tr-012.culturalNotes: Kalburabastı is a traditional Turkish sweet served on special occasions and celebrations.

w-tr-013.title: Kavurma

instructions.1: Add the vegetable oil to a wide pan over high heat.
instructions.2: Add the meat cubes and stir until the meat absorbs its juice and turns brown.
instructions.3: Add the onions and green cayenne pepper and stir until the onions become soft.
instructions.4: Add the tomatoes and stir until they release their juice and become soft.
instructions.5: Add the butter and continue stirring.
instructions.6: Add the salt, black pepper, and red chili pepper flakes and stir for 3 minutes.
instructions.7: Serve the Kavurma hot.

w-tr-013.culturalNotes: Kavurma is a popular dish in Turkey, typically served as a main course.

w-tr-014.title: Grilled Kofta with Zucchini Sauce

instructions.1: Mix the ground beef with the parsley, cilantro, red onion, cinnamon, coriander, cumin, salt, and pepper. Knead the mixture for a few minutes until it becomes well combined.
instructions.2: Shape the mixture into 8 finger-shaped kofta. You can dip your fingers in water to prevent the meat from sticking.
instructions.3: Cover the kofta and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Meanwhile, prepare the zucchini sauce: Sauté the zucchini and garlic in olive oil until slightly browned.
instructions.5: Add the red pepper flakes, herbs, diced tomatoes, salt, and pepper. Add the balsamic vinegar to brighten the flavor. Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes.
instructions.6: Grill the kofta over medium-high heat until cooked through.
instructions.7: Serve the kofta on a large platter with the zucchini sauce. Garnish with more parsley and serve with rice and flatbread.

w-tr-014.culturalNotes: Grilled kofta with zucchini sauce is a popular dish in Turkey, often served with rice and flatbread.

w-tr-015.title: Kumpir - Turkish Stuffed Baked Potatoes

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 200C/400F.
instructions.2: Wrap each potato individually with aluminum foil.
instructions.3: Bake the potatoes for 50 minutes to 1 hour, depending on their size. Test for doneness by inserting a knife into a potato.
instructions.4: Remove the potatoes from the oven, remove the foil, and bake for an additional 5 minutes until the skin is crispy.
instructions.5: Remove the potatoes from the oven and let them cool slightly. Split each potato in the center with a knife, being careful as the inside will be hot.
instructions.6: Use a fork to fluff up the inner flesh without damaging the skin.
instructions.7: Add 1 tablespoon of butter and salt to taste to each potato and mix well.
instructions.8: Gradually add the cheese and keep mixing until it becomes creamy.
instructions.9: Add the toppings as desired and serve hot.

w-tr-015.culturalNotes: Kumpir is a popular dish in Turkey, especially in Istanbul, where it is served as a quick and delicious street food.

w-tr-016.title: Lavash

instructions.1: In a bowl, mix flour, dry yeast, sugar, salt, and warm water and stir them well.
instructions.2: After 10 minutes, melt the butter and let it cool down slightly, then stir it into the bowl and knead the ingredients well.
instructions.3: Cover the bowl with a moistened cloth and let the dough rest for about 40 minutes.
instructions.4: After the dough has rested, flour a counter surface and divide the dough into 6 equal pieces.
instructions.5: Take the first piece and roll it until it is 3-4 mm thick and 18-20 cm in diameter using a rolling pin. Repeat the process with the remaining pieces.
instructions.6: Preheat the oven to 250°C (482°F). Grease the oven tray with a little olive oil and place the first 3 pieces of lavash.
instructions.7: Coat the tops of the dough disks with egg yolk and add the sesame seeds on top. Place the tray into the oven.
instructions.8: Bake for about 10 minutes until the dough puffs up and turns light brown.

w-tr-016.culturalNotes: Lavash is a traditional thin bread in Turkey and is used in many dishes.

w-tr-017.title: Lokum (Turkish Delight)

instructions.1: In a medium saucepan, combine sugar, lemon juice, and 1.5 cups of water. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Reduce heat and simmer until the mixture reaches 240F (soft ball stage). Remove from heat.
instructions.2: In a large saucepan, combine 3/4 cup of water with cornstarch and cream of tartar. Stir until all lumps are removed. Add the remaining 2 cups of water and continue stirring over low heat until the mixture bubbles and becomes thick and glossy.
instructions.3: Ladle a little of the sugar mixture at a time into the cornstarch mixture, whisking continuously until fully incorporated. Continue adding the sugar mixture gradually until the mixture becomes thick and forms ribbons when lifted with a whisk.
instructions.4: Heat the mixture on low for another hour, stirring occasionally. There should be no lumps.
instructions.5: Line two 8x8 inch casseroles with oiled aluminum foil.
instructions.6: Once the mixture is off the heat, divide it into two small bowls. Add rose water and one drop of red food coloring to the first bowl, and orange blossom water and at least 4 drops of yellow food coloring to the second bowl.
instructions.7: Pour each mixture into a separate casserole and let it sit, covered, for 24 hours. Do not refrigerate.
instructions.8: After 24 hours, unmold the candy onto a clean, odor-free cutting board and use an oiled knife to cut it into bite-sized pieces, approximately 1 inch x 1.5 inches.
instructions.9: In a large bowl, whisk together powdered sugar and cornstarch. Place the Turkish Delight in a large casserole filled with half of the coating mixture, then cover with the remaining half.
instructions.10: Let the Turkish Delight stand, covered, for 2 days to develop a crust that keeps the soft, moist interior from sweating outwards.
instructions.11: Enjoy your Turkish Delight! Store leftovers in the coating mixture and do not refrigerate.

w-tr-017.culturalNotes: Lokum is a traditional Turkish sweet known for its delicious taste and smooth texture. It is often served on various occasions and makes a perfect gift.

w-tr-018.title: Turkish Manti

instructions.1: Prepare the dough: In a bowl, mix the flour and salt. Add the egg and lukewarm water gradually, knead until the dough is smooth. Cover the dough and let it rest for 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Prepare the filling: In a bowl, mix the ground lamb, grated onion, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
instructions.3: Make the manti: Roll out the dough into thin circles. Place a small spoonful of the filling in the center of each circle, then seal them to form pouches. Place the manti in a pot of boiling water for 15-20 minutes until cooked.
instructions.4: Prepare the yogurt sauce: In a bowl, mix the yogurt, garlic, salt, and pepper. Set aside.
instructions.5: Prepare the oil/butter sauce: In a pan, melt the olive oil or butter. Add the Aleppo pepper flakes and stir for a minute.
instructions.6: Add the cooked manti to the yogurt sauce, then pour the oil/butter sauce on top. Serve hot.

w-tr-018.culturalNotes: Manti is a traditional Turkish dish often served on special occasions and family gatherings.

w-tr-019.title: Menemen (Eggs with Onion, Green Pepper, and Tomato)

instructions.1: Prepare a concassée of tomatoes by blanching, peeling, seeding, and dicing the tomatoes. Alternatively, you may use a food processor or box grater.
instructions.2: Dice the onions and green peppers into medium-sized cubes and sauté them in the olive oil until tender.
instructions.3: Add the oregano and paprika, if using.
instructions.4: Add the tomatoes to the onions and green peppers and cook for 5 minutes.
instructions.5: Add the parsley and season with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
instructions.6: Beat the eggs in a bowl and pour them over the mixture in the pan. Stir gently until the eggs are cooked.
instructions.7: Serve with Turkish bread.

w-tr-019.culturalNotes: Menemen is a traditional Turkish breakfast dish, typically served with fresh bread.

w-tr-020.title: Muhallebi with Pistachios and Rose Water

w-tr-020-i6.name: rose water or orange flower water

instructions.1: Mix the milk and sugar in a large saucepan and heat slowly to avoid burning the milk, then bring to a simmer.
instructions.2: Make a slurry by dissolving the rice flour and cornstarch in the water, then slowly add this mixture to the simmering milk while stirring constantly.
instructions.3: Simmer gently for 30-40 minutes, stirring frequently, until the mixture has thickened enough to coat a spoon. Remove from the heat.
instructions.4: Stir in the rose water or orange flower water.
instructions.5: Pour the mixture into a 9x13-inch baking pan and refrigerate until chilled and set.
instructions.6: Cut the mixture into 4-inch squares.
instructions.7: Place the squares on individual dessert plates and garnish with the chopped pistachios.

w-tr-020.culturalNotes: Muhallebi is a traditional Turkish dessert served on special occasions and celebrations.

w-tr-021.title: Muhammara

instructions.1: Grill the red bell peppers until they are charred and softened.
instructions.2: Set the peppers aside for 15 minutes in a covered bowl to steam.
instructions.3: Remove the skins, seeds, and stems from the peppers.
instructions.4: Add all the ingredients to a blender and blend until smooth.
instructions.5: Serve the muhammara chilled or warm.

w-tr-021.culturalNotes: Muhammara is a popular dish in Turkey, Syria, and Lebanon, typically served as a dip with bread or vegetables.

w-tr-022.title: Azeri Saffron Pilaf with Potato Kazmag

instructions.1: Slice the potatoes thinly.
instructions.2: Mix water with 4 tablespoons of melted butter. Pour the mixture into the bottom of a large skillet with a tight-fitting lid.
instructions.3: Arrange the potato slices on the bottom of the skillet, fitting them close together without overlapping. Cook over medium heat for 5-10 minutes until the potatoes soften and begin to turn slightly golden.
instructions.4: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold water to remove the starch.
instructions.5: Cover the rice with warm water by an inch. Add 2 teaspoons of salt and let it soak for about an hour.
instructions.6: Drain the water and rinse the rice again.
instructions.7: Add the rice to a large pot of boiling, salted water (about 3 quarts of water). Boil for about 8 minutes, or until slightly hard still – almost cooked.
instructions.8: Drain and rinse the rice again.
instructions.9: Add half the rice to the casserole, sprinkle with 4 tablespoons of melted butter, and top with the second half of the rice. Add another 4 tablespoons of melted butter.
instructions.10: Use the handle of a wooden spoon to poke 6 holes into the rice for steam to travel through. Cover with the lid and weigh down with cans to help seal steam in, if necessary.
instructions.11: Cook the pilaf over low heat for about 40 minutes, weighing down the lid so that no steam can escape.
instructions.12: Spoon 2 cups of cooked pilaf into a small bowl. Toss with saffron and the final 4 tablespoons of butter.
instructions.13: Spoon the plain pilaf onto a serving platter. Add the saffron rice on top.
instructions.14: Using a good wooden spoon or spatula, scrape the potato 'crust' off the pan. Sprinkle the crust over the top of the pilaf.
instructions.15: Garnish with fresh mint if desired. Serve immediately.

w-tr-022.culturalNotes: Azeri Saffron Pilaf with Potato Kazmag is a traditional dish in Azerbaijan, often served on special occasions.

w-tr-023.title: Cardamom & Rose Water Custard | Firnee

instructions.1: Heat the milk in a small, heavy-bottomed saucepan over low heat.
instructions.2: In a small cup, mix the cornstarch with a few tablespoons of milk. Stir until you get a smooth, gravy-like consistency. This is called a cornstarch slurry.
instructions.3: Add the cornstarch slurry, sugar, cardamom, and rose water to the saucepan. Stir constantly until the mixture thickens and a few bubbles break through the surface - about 5-10 minutes.
instructions.4: Remove from heat and ladle into serving dishes. This recipe will fill 4 small ramekins.
instructions.5: Cover the dishes with plastic wrap, pressing it lightly onto the pudding to prevent a skin from forming.
instructions.6: Refrigerate and cool completely - for at least an hour.

w-tr-023.culturalNotes: Cardamom and rose water custard is a traditional Turkish dessert, known for its aromatic flavor and creamy texture.

w-th-001.title: Coconut Banana Fritters

instructions.1: Fill a large pot or high-sided skillet halfway with vegetable oil. Heat the oil to 375F.
instructions.2: Meanwhile, whisk together the batter ingredients in a bowl. Add the chopped bananas and mash them well using a potato masher or similar.
instructions.3: When the oil reaches 375F, scoop some of the batter into the hot oil. Be careful not to splash. Use an ice cream scoop to gently place the batter in the oil.
instructions.4: Fry the fritters until they are deep golden brown, turning as needed.
instructions.5: When done, place the fritters on paper towels to absorb excess oil.
instructions.6: Dust the fritters with powdered sugar and serve immediately.

w-th-001.culturalNotes: Coconut banana fritters are a popular dessert in Thailand, often served as a snack or after-meal treat.

w-th-002.title: Bubble Tea Noodles in Coconut Milk (Lod Chong Singapore/Cendol)

instructions.1: Make the syrup: Combine the sugar and 1 ¼ cup of coconut water or water in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the pandan leaf and bring to a boil for 5 minutes. Remove from heat and let the syrup cool.
instructions.2: Make the coconut milk: Combine the coconut milk, ½ cup of coconut water, and ⅛ tsp of salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the pandan leaf and bring to a boil for 5 minutes. Remove from heat and let the coconut milk cool.
instructions.3: Make the noodles: In a bowl, mix the tapioca starch and mung bean starch. Add ⅔ cup of water and 5 drops of green food coloring, and knead until the mixture is smooth. Let the dough rest for 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Shape the noodles: Roll out the dough on a surface dusted with tapioca starch. Cut the dough into thin strips and cook them in boiling water for 2 minutes until they become translucent. Remove the strips from the water and rinse them under cold water.
instructions.5: If serving right away: Place the strips in glasses and pour the syrup and coconut milk over them. Add the sweet jackfruit and ice, and serve cold.
instructions.6: If not serving right away: Store the strips in a plastic-covered bowl in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Follow the previous steps when ready to serve.

w-th-002.culturalNotes: Lod Chong is a popular sweet dish in Thailand, Malaysia, and Singapore, typically served in small cold glasses.

w-th-003.title: Halal Sausage Fried Rice

instructions.1: Add the halal chicken sausage to a wok and spread out into a single layer. Turn heat on medium high and let them cook without stirring until they start to brown on one side and render a little bit of fat. Toss the sausage and keep cooking briefly just to cook them through. Do not cook them for too long or you will render out too much fat and cause the sausage to become too salty. Remove from heat, then remove the sausage from the pan, leaving any rendered fat behind.
instructions.2: Add more oil to coat the bottom of the pan. Turn the heat on medium and add onions and carrots and cook for about 2 minutes or until onions are translucent. Add garlic and cook for another 30 seconds, then add gai lan and toss just until wilted.
instructions.3: Push veggies to one side to create space for the eggs, and move the wok so the veggies are sitting a bit off the element. If the pan is dry, you can add a bit more oil for the eggs here. Add the eggs and break the yolks, then let them set about half way.
instructions.4: Scramble briefly, then add the rice and pour the soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar and white pepper onto the rice and toss everything together briefly.
instructions.5: Add the sausage back in and continue tossing until the rice is all separated and evenly coated in the sauce.
instructions.6: Once well mixed, let the rice sit without stirring for 10-15 seconds to toast slightly, then toss to mix and let it toast again. Do this 3 times, or more if your rice is a bit moist, until the rice is dry and some of the grains have browned.
instructions.7: Remove from heat and plate. Top with some chopped cilantro or green onions and serve with fresh cucumber slices. You can also squeeze a bit of lime over it to cut the richness.

w-th-003.culturalNotes: Halal Sausage Fried Rice is a popular dish in Thai cuisine, typically served as a main course.

w-th-004.title: Green Papaya Curry

instructions.1: Peel the papaya from the narrow end, leaving a bit unpeeled at the top for a grip. Cut the papaya in half and scoop out the seeds. Cube it.
instructions.2: In a large pan over medium heat, add the oil, onion, garlic, and Thai bird chili (if using). Cook until the onion is soft.
instructions.3: Add the curry powder, papaya, coconut milk, and salt. Cover and simmer until the papaya is tender (about 15 minutes).
instructions.4: Serve the curry with a heaping bowl of rice.

w-th-004.culturalNotes: Green Papaya Curry is a delicious dish from Thai cuisine, known for its sweet and spicy flavors.

w-th-005.title: Green Papaya Salad

instructions.1: Peel the green papaya and shred it into thin slices.
instructions.2: Wash the green onions and slice them thinly.
instructions.3: Place all the ingredients in a large bowl.
instructions.4: Add the lime juice and vegetable oil, and toss well.
instructions.5: Season with salt and black pepper to taste, and toss again.
instructions.6: Serve the salad cold.

w-th-005.culturalNotes: Green papaya salad is a famous dish in Thailand, known for its tangy and salty flavor.

w-th-006.title: Hainanese Chicken Rice (Khao Mun Gai)

w-th-006-i4.name: jasmine rice
w-th-006-i4.standardAmount: 1 1/2 cups (rinsed until the water runs clear and drained well)

instructions.1: Trim extra fat and skin off your chicken thighs and reserve. You will need to render fat from these trimmings for the rice.
instructions.2: Sprinkle salt over chicken and rub it in. Let sit at room temp while you prep other things.
instructions.3: In a wok, or the pot you're using to cook the rice in, add just a tiny bit of vegetable oil along with chicken fat/skin trimmings. Saute over medium-low heat to render chicken fat until the trimmings are browned. You want to have about 2 Tbsp of fat total, so if there is too much, remove some. If there isn't enough, add a little more vegetable oil to supplement. Remove chicken trimmings, leaving the fat in the pot.
instructions.4: In the same pot/wok you used to render chicken fat, add chopped ginger and garlic and saute over medium high heat until garlic starts to turn golden.
instructions.5: Add raw, rinsed rice and salt, and turn heat up to high, tossing rice for about 2 minutes until hot throughout and dry.
instructions.6: Transfer rice into a rice cooker or a heavy bottomed pot (unless you're already using that pot). Add chicken stock to the rice and stir to mix. Place chicken in one layer on top of rice.
instructions.7: Turn heat to high and watch until you start to see the first sign of simmering. Then turn the heat down to low, cover with a tight fitting lid and cook for 25 minutes or until the chicken is done.
instructions.8: When chicken is cooked, remove chicken from the rice and let rest for at least 5 minutes before slicing.
instructions.9: Fluff rice to distribute seasoning and chicken juices evenly.
instructions.10: To serve: Slice chicken into thin pieces, and place on top of rice. Serve with dipping sauce, some fresh cucumber and extra chicken broth as soup. Enjoy!

w-th-006.culturalNotes: Hainanese chicken rice is a popular dish in Thailand, also known as 'Khao Mun Gai'. It is typically served with a dipping sauce and fresh cucumber.

w-th-007.title: Thai Coconut Pancakes (Kanom Krok)

instructions.1: Place all ingredients for the shell, except the oil for greasing, in a blender and blend until smooth.
instructions.2: Whisk the rice flour, sugar, and salt together until there are no more clumps of flour. Add coconut milk and whisk until sugar is dissolved.
instructions.3: Prepare the toppings and a cooling rack.
instructions.4: Heat the pan at 325°F if there are temp controls, or over medium heat for stovetop. Test the pan for readiness by sprinkling a bit of water onto the pan; if it sizzles away immediately, it's hot enough.
instructions.5: Brush half the holes with the oil. Use a small spoon to spoon about ½ a tablespoon of the shell batter into the pre-heated, oiled holes.
instructions.6: Use a heatproof measuring spoon to add 1 teaspoon of the filling by dunking the bottom of the teaspoon right into the middle of the shell, and wiggle it slightly as you pour in the batter.
instructions.7: Let them cook for a minute or two, then add your toppings. If the toppings sink too much into the cakes, it means the cakes are not cooked enough.
instructions.8: Continue to let them cook until the bottom is crispy and golden brown, and the top is no longer runny, about 5 minutes. If the bottom is done but the top still needs more cooking, cover the pan with a pot lid or a baking sheet for a minute.
instructions.9: Remove the cakes by scooping them out with a small spoon and placing them on a cooling rack. If your pan has a nonstick coating, you may want to use a wooden skewer or toothpick to push them up, then use a spoon to lift them out.
instructions.10: Let them cool for a few minutes before eating, or you will burn your mouth! Eat them while they're still warm as they get soggy quickly. If they have gone cold and soggy, put them back into the pan over medium heat for a few minutes until you hear them sizzle for about a minute.

w-th-007.culturalNotes: Kanom Krok is a traditional Thai dessert usually served as a snack or after-meal treat.
